q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a PPE coverall?
title: PPE coverall carbon footprint per piece
short: Weigh the non-woven or laminated fabric per coverall and multiply by its supplier figure, then add zips, elastic and tape. Add cutting, stitching and seam sealing electricity, divide by coveralls passed and add packing.
audience: PPE kit makers and hospital buyers

ul: Polypropylene non-woven or laminated fabric by weight.
Zip, elastic and seam sealing tape.
Folding, packing and sterilising if required.

p: Report per coverall with its fabric weight in GSM and size. The fabric usually carries most of the footprint.

example.title: Worked example: PPE coverall unit per piece (one month)
lines: Plant total: 7,100 / 100,000 = 0.0710 kg CO2 per piece
Add fabric and trims for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
